title: Higher-order convex-concave saddle-point problems: complete scalar jets and global gap
summary: Solve $\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}f(x,y)$, with $K=X\times Y$ and $z=(x,y)$. The target is the global saddle-point gap.

description_paragraphs: Solve $\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}f(x,y)$, with $K=X\times Y$ and $z=(x,y)$. The target is the global saddle-point gap.

assumptions.description: The conditions $f\in C^p$ and $\|\nabla^p f(z)-\nabla^p f(w)\|\le L_p\|z-w\|$ hold on a neighborhood of the product domain, with $p\ge2$ fixed.
The feasible domain is nonempty, compact, and convex, with $\operatorname{diam}(K)\le D_K$; for saddle problems, $K=X\times Y$.

model.parameter_domain_description: $D_K$: positive real; $L_p$: positive real; $d$: integer at least 2; $\varepsilon$: positive real; $p$: integer at least 2. Derived quantities are defined in the parameter table. Each region states any additional accuracy and dimension conditions.
description_paragraphs: The sets $X\subset\mathbb R^{d_x}$ and $Y\subset\mathbb R^{d_y}$ are known, nonempty, compact, and convex; $K=X\times Y\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d=d_x+d_y$, and $\operatorname{diam}(K)\le D_K$. Queries and outputs lie in $K$; differentiability holds on an open neighborhood of $K$.
Fix an integer $p\ge2$. The function $f$ is convex on $x$ and concave on $y$; assume $f\in C^p$ and $\|\nabla^p f(z)-\nabla^p f(w)\|_{\rm op}\le L_p\|z-w\|_2$.
These conditions ensure existence of a solution. Derivative tensors use the multilinear operator norm induced by the Euclidean norm.

objects.definition: The unknown real-valued payoff is $f:X\times Y\to\mathbb R$, where $X\subset\mathbb R^{d_x}$ and $Y\subset\mathbb R^{d_y}$. All required derivatives are defined on a neighborhood of the product domain.
The derived saddle operator is $F_f(x,y)=(\nabla_x f(x,y),-\nabla_y f(x,y))\in\mathbb R^{d_x+d_y}$.
The feasible set is explicitly public. Exact projections and linear algebra use known geometry and reveal no hidden-function information.

norms.definition: Euclidean norm and inner product are $\|v\|_2=(\sum_jv_j^2)^{1/2}$ and $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_j u_jv_j$. The joint space uses $\|(x,y)\|_2=(\|x\|_2^2+\|y\|_2^2)^{1/2}$. Multilinear derivative tensors carry the induced operator norm.

conditions: The operator $F_f=(\nabla_xf,-\nabla_yf)$ is monotone and its derivative $\mathrm D^{p-1}F_f$ has Lipschitz bound $L_p$. One full scalar jet of order p yields the complete operator jet through order p-1 without extra calls.
Use the actual monotone-VI algorithm and its output certificate. Proposition 3.6 of the scalar saddle-point source provides the structural map for the derived operator.

On the product domain, convexity-concavity bounds global saddle gap by $D_K\operatorname{dist}(0,F_f(z)+N_K(z))$. Run at internal tangent tolerance $\varepsilon/D_K$, giving $\chi_{\rm gap}=L_pD_K^{p+1}/\varepsilon$.

bounds.derivation: Let $S=\operatorname{diag}(I,-I)$ and $F=S\nabla f$. One scalar jet of order $p$ constructs $(F,\mathrm DF,\ldots,\mathrm D^{p-1}F)$ with the same $L_p$. Tangent residual transfers directly; by $\operatorname{Gap}\le D_K r_{\rm tan}$, a gap target uses residual tolerance $\varepsilon/D_K$. Combine the reduction in Proposition 3.6 with Theorem 3.1 of arXiv:2609.23557. This supplies no additional free oracle access to the unknown object.

notes: The source scalar-payoff hard family directly covers arbitrary randomized algorithms. A general vector-VI lower bound is not converted backward to a saddle lower bound without a construction.

Let $T$ denote the outer iteration count. Lemma 5.4 and (22)-(23) sum all inner-solver calls to obtain total inner cost $O(T)$. The counted object is a full jet call, so outer iterations alone are insufficient. Bound the source initial distance to a solution by the domain diameter $D_K$.
